title: When No Allele Hides the Other

scenes.tts: Cross a red snapdragon with a white one. In the classic textbook example, every offspring has pink flowers. Breed a red Shorthorn cow with a white bull. The calf is roan. Its coat has red hairs and white hairs side by side. These do not fit the old rule, where a dominant allele hides a recessive one. What is going on?
scenes.visual: Red and white snapdragon swatches cross to a pink swatch; red and white cattle swatches cross to a roan swatch of mixed hairs; a question mark and the essential question appear.
scenes.narration: Cross a red snapdragon with a white one. In the classic textbook example, every offspring has pink flowers. Breed a red Shorthorn cow with a white bull. The calf is roan. Its coat has red hairs and white hairs side by side. These do not fit the old rule, where a dominant allele hides a recessive one. What is going on?

scenes.tts: An allele is one version of a gene. A heterozygous plant has two different alleles. For snapdragon color, R is the red allele, and W is the white allele. R R is red, W W is white, and R W is pink. This is incomplete dominance. The heterozygote shows a color in between.

scenes.visual: Allele tokens R (red) and W (white); three genotype chips RR, WW, RW with their colour swatches; the RW pink swatch sits between red and white on a bar labelled incomplete dominance.
scenes.narration: An allele is one version of a gene. A heterozygous plant has two different alleles. For snapdragon color, R is the red allele, and W is the white allele. RR is red, WW is white, and RW is pink. This is incomplete dominance. The heterozygote shows a color in between.

scenes.tts: Think of mixing paint. But paint stays mixed. A pink plant passes a separate R or W to each sex cell. Cross two pink plants, and the Punnett square gives one red, two pink, and one white. Red and white come back. The alleles never blended.
scenes.visual: Two pink RW plants send separate R and W tokens into a 2 by 2 Punnett square; the four cells fill RR red, RW pink, RW pink, WW white; the 1 : 2 : 1 ratio appears; red and white cells pulse.
scenes.narration: Think of mixing paint. But paint stays mixed. A pink plant passes a separate R or W to each sex cell. Cross two pink plants, and the Punnett square gives one red, two pink, and one white. Red and white come back. The alleles never blended.

scenes.tts: Codominance means both alleles show fully in the heterozygote. In Shorthorn cattle, R W is roan. Each hair is red or white, and the two kinds grow side by side. A roan by roan cross gives one red, two roan, one white, on average. Human A B O blood type is another case. Red blood cells can carry an A marker, a B marker, both, or neither. Type A B carries both.
scenes.caption: Codominance means both alleles show fully in the heterozygote. In Shorthorn cattle, RW is roan. Each hair is red or white, and the two kinds grow side by side. A roan by roan cross gives 1 red, 2 roan, 1 white, on average. Human ABO blood type is another case. Red blood cells can carry an A marker, a B marker, both, or neither. Type AB carries both.
scenes.visual: A roan swatch made of red and white hair bars beside a pink swatch for contrast; the 1 : 2 : 1 roan ratio; then four blood-cell outlines labelled type A, B, AB, O with A and B marker chips on them.
scenes.narration: Codominance means both alleles show fully in the heterozygote. In Shorthorn cattle, RW is roan. Each hair is red or white, and the two kinds grow side by side. scenes.tts: Geneticists study existing families. A pedigree is a chart of a family. A shaded symbol is a person who shows the trait. Two unshaded parents with a shaded child are a clue for a recessive trait, not proof. A karyotype is a picture of a cell's chromosomes, sorted into pairs. A typical human body cell with a nucleus has 46 chromosomes. Three copies of chromosome 21 is called trisomy 21, and a cell with it has 47 chromosomes.
scenes.visual: A three-generation pedigree built from squares and circles, two unshaded parents and one shaded child highlighted; then the pedigree slides away and 23 pairs of chromosome bars appear, labelled 46; a third bar joins pair 21 and the count becomes 47.

A typical human body cell with a nucleus has 46 chromosomes. Three copies of chromosome 21 is called trisomy 21, and a cell with it has 47 chromosomes.

scenes.tts: So what if neither allele is fully dominant? In incomplete dominance, the heterozygote is in between. In codominance, it shows both alleles. Either way, the alleles stay separate, and red and white offspring return. Pedigrees and karyotypes let us follow traits through families and chromosomes.
scenes.visual: The question is restated; two cards, incomplete dominance (RW pink, in between) and codominance (RW both colours), each with separate R and W tokens beneath, and the answer line.
